subject: Chemistry
title: Alkanes: Core Synthetic Routes & Reaction Mechanisms
topics: Wurtz Reaction (2RX + 2Na → R-R in dry ether; Symmetrical alkanes only; Methane cannot be prepared)
Kolbe's Electrolysis (2RCOOK → R-R + 2CO₂ at Anode; H₂ at Cathode; pH rises)
Corey-House Synthesis (Gilman Reagent R₂CuLi + R'X → R-R'; Unsymmetrical alkanes)
Decarboxylation with Soda-Lime (RCOONa + NaOH/CaO → R-H + Na₂CO₃; 1 carbon less)
quickSummary: Wurtz for symmetrical even-carbon alkanes. Kolbe's electrolysis yields R-R at anode. Corey-House (Gilman reagent R₂CuLi) synthesizes unsymmetrical alkanes cleanly. Decarboxylation yields alkanes with 1 less carbon.
summary: Master core laboratory and industrial synthetic routes for alkanes: Wurtz, Kolbe, Corey-House, and Decarboxylation.

summaryBox.title: Synthetic Routes
summaryBox.takeaway: Wurtz (even C, symmetrical), Kolbe (anodic R-R + CO₂), Corey-House (unsymmetrical R-R'), Decarboxylation (1 less C).

conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
ALKANE SYNTHETIC ROUTES
                                        │
     ┌──────────────────┬───────────────┼───────────────┬──────────────────┐
     ▼                  ▼               ▼               ▼                  ▼
WURTZ REACTION      KOLBE ELECTROLYSIS  COREY-HOUSE     DECARBOXYLATION    DECARBONYLATION
2RX + 2Na →         Aqueous RCOOK       Gilman Reagent  RCOONa + NaOH      Reductants on
R-R + 2NaX          at Anode →          R₂CuLi + R'X    → R-H              Aldehydes/Ketones
(Symmetrical).      R-R + 2CO₂.         → R-R'.         (1 C less).        (Clemmensen/Wolf).
conceptBreakdown.content:
• **Wurtz Reaction**: $2\text{RX} + 2\text{Na} \xrightarrow{\text{dry ether}} R-R + 2\text{NaX}$. Best for symmetrical alkanes with even carbon counts. Cross-Wurtz gives a mixture of three alkanes. **Methane CANNOT be prepared**.
• **Kolbe's Electrolysis**: Electrolysis of aqueous sodium/potassium carboxylates. Free radical oxidation at the **Anode** yields $R-R + 2\text{CO}_2$; **Cathode** yields $\text{H}_2$ gas (alkaline $\text{KOH}$ accumulates around cathode).
• **Corey-House Synthesis**: $R_2\text{CuLi} + R'\text{X} \to R-R' + R\text{Cu} + \text{LiX}$. Clean coupling of unsymmetrical alkanes via Lithium dialkylcuprates (**Gilman Reagents**).
• **Decarboxylation**: $R\text{COONa} + \text{NaOH} \xrightarrow{\text{CaO}, \Delta} R-\text{H} + \text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3$. Soda-lime ($	ext{NaOH}:\text{CaO} = 3:1$) yields an alkane with **one carbon less**.

quickRevision: Methane cannot be prepared by Wurtz or Kolbe electrolysis.
Corey-House is ideal for unsymmetrical alkanes.
In Kolbe electrolysis, R-R and CO₂ evolve at the anode; H₂ at the cathode.
Decarboxylation with soda-lime reduces chain length by 1 carbon.
